title: Symbolic World Models
lines: Symbolic World Models explores how systems preserve meaning as situations change.
Its proposal connects explicit situations, revisable reasons, and actions checked against reality.
That gives readers a way to question what an apparently fluent answer actually depends on.

Reveal a question marker over the links, inviting inspection of what supports an answer.

title: A change travels
lines: Move a departure to Friday, and a previously feasible meeting may become impossible.
Here, the trip is a world instance; reusable relationships belong to a world pattern.
Changing the arrival updates the dependent conclusion, instead of simply replacing yesterday’s sentence.
cues: Reveal a Friday calendar, a train and the meeting it might affect.
Reveal a smaller abstract relationship pattern beneath the particular trip.
Trace the arrival-to-meeting dependency and reveal May conflict, preserving the conditional claim.

title: Remember the reasons
lines: To follow changes, the book preserves the reasons supporting each conclusion.
A justified conclusion can lose one supporting route while another still holds.
That distinction explains why remembering reasons matters as much as remembering an answer.
cues: Reveal two separate evidence routes to one supported conclusion.
Withdraw the first route and mark its premise corrected, keeping the other route visible.
Emphasize the surviving connection and the question What still supports it?

title: Prediction and confirmation
lines: In a connected room, predicted warmth is different from a measured temperature.
Sending a heating command is different again from confirming its physical effect.
These examples develop an architecture for keeping interpretation, reasoning, and execution connected.
cues: Reveal a room with separately identified Observation and Prediction thermometers.
Draw the command toward the heater, with a pending confirmation symbol rather than a success check.
Connect the example to the three abstract roles Interpret, Reason and Verify.
